title: Associated primes of a flat tensor lie in the corresponding residue-field fibre
statement: Let $R\to S$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, with $R$ and $S$ Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let $P$ be a finite $S$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] flat over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. For every finite $R$-module $Q$ and every prime $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Ass}_S(Q\otimes_R P)$, put $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap R$. Then $\mathfrak q$ is an associated prime of the fibre module $P\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, regarded as an $S$-module through its canonical action; equivalently, under the standard identification of primes of $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ with primes of $S$ lying over $\mathfrak p$, it belongs to $\operatorname{Ass}_{S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)}(P\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$. Here associated primes are annihilators of elements [def-weil-pbc-annihilator-associated-primes], and $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is the residue field [def-weil-residue-field]. Tensor products are [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product].

source.place: Tags 05C2 (lemma-bourbaki-fibres), statement and proof, together with Tag 05E0 (remark-bourbaki), lines 15880-15916

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-associated-primes-flat-base-change] with $M=Q$ and $N=P$. The equality clause applies because $R$ is Noetherian and $P$ is $R$-flat. It supplies a prime $\mathfrak p_0\in\operatorname{Ass}_R(Q)$ such that $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Ass}_S(P/\mathfrak p_0P)$. Choose a witness $z\in P/\mathfrak p_0P$ with $\operatorname{Ann}_S(z)=\mathfrak q$. The witness is nonzero, since the annihilator of zero is the whole ring and $\mathfrak q$ is proper.

source.place: Tag 0312 (lemma-bourbaki), equality; Tag 05C2 (lemma-bourbaki-fibres), proof reduction to the prime quotient

proof.text: Write $\varphi:R\to S$ for the given homomorphism and check $\mathfrak p_0=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. Every $a\in\mathfrak p_0$ kills the quotient, hence kills $z$. Conversely, for $a\notin\mathfrak p_0$, multiplication by $a$ on $R/\mathfrak p_0$ is injective: $ar\in\mathfrak p_0$ forces $r\in\mathfrak p_0$ by primality. Tensor this injection with $P$, using [lem-weil-pbc-flat-tensor-exact]. Under the quotient-tensor isomorphism of [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring], the resulting map is multiplication by $a$ on $P/\mathfrak p_0P$ (on $\bar r\otimes y$ both maps give $ary$ modulo $\mathfrak p_0P$). Thus $\varphi(a)z=0$ would imply $z=0$, a contradiction. This proves the contraction equality and identifies $\mathfrak p_0$ with the statement's $\mathfrak p$.

source.place: Tag 05C2 via Tag 05C1 (lemma-post-bourbaki), the nonzerodivisor calculation on the prime quotient, written out using flat tensor exactness

proof.text: Write $\varphi:R\to S$ for the given homomorphism. Apply [lem-trf-fibre-module-localization] to $A=R$, $B=S$, $N=P$, and the now identified prime $\mathfrak p$. Its canonical $S$-linear isomorphism identifies $(\varphi(R\setminus\mathfrak p))^{-1}(P/\mathfrak pP)$ with $P\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Its annihilator clause applies to the witness $z$ from Step 1 because Step 2 established $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)=\mathfrak p$. Hence the image of $z/1$ in the fibre has $S$-annihilator exactly $\mathfrak q$. This proves the first assertion directly with an element witness.

source.place: Tag 05C2, localization of the prime quotient as in Tag 05C1; Tag 05BZ (lemma-localize-ass), witness localization

proof.text: Put $C=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $L=P\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, with $(s\otimes\lambda)(y\otimes\mu)=sy\otimes\lambda\mu$. This balanced formula defines the canonical $C$-action and restricts to the original $S$-action. Apply [lem-trf-fibre-associated-primes-module-ring] to this $C$-module. It says that $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Ass}_S(L)$ if and only if the corresponding prime $\mathfrak Q$ of $C$ lies in $\operatorname{Ass}_C(L)$, and explicitly transports annihilators of the same element. Applied to Step 3, this is exactly the equivalently clause of the item.
